assembledMessages.content: In one short paragraph: why might booked COGS diverge from cash-verified supplier invoice cost? Reason carefully before answering.

output: Booked COGS is typically a system-generated figure — derived from standard costs, moving averages, or the last PO price at time of receipt — and gets posted at the point of sale or period-end accrual, often before the actual supplier invoice arrives. Cash-verified invoice cost is the real, settled amount, which can differ due to: price variances (the invoice reflects a negotiated/final price different from the standard or PO estimate), timing mismatches (goods received and COGS booked in one period, invoice paid in another, especially with freight, duty, or rebates added later), FX rate differences if the invoice is in a foreign currency and booked at a different rate than paid, partial shipments or short-pays/deductions changing the cash amount, and manual journal adjustments or accruals that were estimated rather than tied to the actual invoice. In short, the divergence is usually a timing/estimation gap between accrual accounting (COGS) and cash accounting (invoice payment), not necessarily an error — but it should still be reconciled and any unexplained variance flagged `[VERIFY]` rather than assumed.
